Claim: Acute caffeine partially mitigated selected sleep-loss vigilance, cognition and military-task decrements in the reviewed military trials; this does not resolve sleep loss or establish benefit for every task.
Population: Military personnel or military-related populations under sleep deprivation, sleep restriction, or sustained wakefulness
Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials
Disposition_Rationale: Sleep/caffeine is task-dependent and International-only; one review supports a bounded supporting section, not broad readiness advice.

Claim: In the sampled PMDF cohort of male officers older than 40 years, measured cardiometabolic risk burden supported consideration of surveillance; the cross-sectional study did not identify confirmed role or shift differences.
Population: Active-duty male Federal District Military Police officers aged >40 years without known atherosclerotic disease
Disposition_Rationale: Direct, result-located Brazilian medical-readiness evidence; International use remains transferability context only.

Claim: In the studied military-police sample, leisure-time physical activity had weak cross-sectional discrimination for absence of low-back pain; it does not establish prevention or an operational cutoff.
Population: Military police from four units in Jequié, Bahia, Brazil
Disposition_Rationale: Weak cross-sectional discrimination; retain only to delimit musculoskeletal inference.

Claim: In one small police-cadet comparison, shooting score, time and accuracy coefficient did not differ significantly by the reported stress-symptom grouping.
In the overlapping police-cadet cohort, the displayed physical-activity and several fitness measures did not show statistically significant correlations with shooting outcomes.
Locator: Table 3; physical activity and physical-fitness rows
Population: 26 military police officers in the Espírito Santo Officer Training Course
Disposition_Rationale: Null correlations are useful, but cohort overlaps RC-BRA-SHOOT-01 and count as one independent cohort.

Claim: A military-police record review documented more tourniquet applications in 2020–2024 than in 2013–2017; it does not establish a training effect or patient outcome.
Population: REDS occurrences documenting police application of a tourniquet in Minas Gerais
Disposition_Rationale: Descriptive tactical-medicine record evidence; no training or patient-outcome inference.

Claim: The evaluated Escola Segura implementation showed no statistically significant effect on the listed outcomes in the studied school setting.
Locator: Results, Table 4 and first Results interpretation paragraph on p.16
Population: One Escola Segura treatment school compared with one control school; survey respondents
Disposition_Rationale: Null implementation evaluation is retained for organizational context.

Claim: A PMPI documentary case identified service constraints and proposed a policy plan; it is organizational context, not evidence of clinical effectiveness.
Population: PMPI CAIS institutional documents and open information
Disposition_Rationale: Documentary institutional proposal, not effectiveness evidence.

Claim: In a Paraná occupational cohort, selected health conditions were associated with medical non-readiness; this association does not establish causality.
Disposition_Rationale: Large Paraná occupational cohort supports a bounded medical non-readiness section.

Claim: In a systematic review of 16 controlled military studies, dietary-supplement findings were inconsistent and mostly modest, and the authors judged practical field-performance guidance inadequate.
Design: Systematic review of randomized and quasi-experimental controlled trials
Boundary: Does not justify a general supplementation protocol, causal field-readiness claim, or direct transfer to Brazilian public safety.
Disposition_Rationale: Nutrition/supplementation is an unresolved core gap and EV-0140 remains unadjudicated contradictory evidence.

Claim: In 30 male firefighters receiving protein-carbohydrate regimens, adding creatine was associated with larger improvements in rescue and forcible-entry task times; several other tasks and total time showed no group-time interaction.
Boundary: Does not show that protein/carbohydrate alone caused benefit, that every occupational task improved, or that results generalize to female firefighters or Brazilian agencies.
Disposition_Rationale: Nutrition/supplementation is removed from core scope.

Claim: In 216 recruits followed for 12 months at one Chinese police academy, higher graduation-stage composite fitness was associated with higher supervisor-rated job performance and lower musculoskeletal-injury hazard; the cohort does not establish a causal effect of testing or conditioning.
Locator: Results Table 1 and multivariable regression results; Limitations.
Population: 216 followed recruits at one Chinese police academy
Boundary: Does not prove that fitness testing, assignment, or conditioning causes lower injury or better performance.
Disposition_Rationale: Physical fitness/academy readiness is an unresolved core gap with unresolved contradictory HIGH evidence.

Claim: Among 34 Slovenian infantry personnel, end-running speed, maximal heart rate and predicted VO2max from the 30-15 intermittent fitness test showed test-retest ICCs of 0.971, 0.960 and 0.975, respectively; this does not validate a readiness score or operational prediction in other populations.
Boundary: Does not validate the test for Brazilian policing, establish combat readiness, or prove outcome prediction beyond this small infantry cohort.
Disposition_Rationale: Physical fitness/academy readiness is removed from core scope.

Claim: In one small cross-sectional sample of Brazilian military police officers, administrative and tactical-force groups did not differ significantly in weekly physical-activity time or reported musculoskeletal discomfort; the finding is contextual and does not establish occupational, behavioral, or preventive effects.
Population: 31 Brazilian military police officers (administrative n=15; tactical force n=16)
Boundary: No causal, prospective, preventive, readiness-score, or national-generalization claim.
Disposition_Rationale: Located Brazilian null result; small cross-sectional sample, contextual only.
